label: TP
reason: Both alerts represent real vulnerabilities. Alert 2 (SQL injection) at L68 shows user input flows directly into the SQL query string without sanitization (bar ← param ← user-requested-param-name). Alert 1 (XSS) at L73-L74 involves the same data flow reaching HTML output via encodeForHTML, but per balanced encoding guidance, attacker-controlled data reaching the sink despite encoding warrants alert-TP. Neither alert proves the resolved sink value is a constant/non-user string.

evidence.note: User parameter name captured into param variable
param passed to doSomething and assigned to bar (switch target 'C')
SQL injection sink: bar (containing user input) concatenated into sql query
XSS sink: sql containing user input printed via encodeForHTML
